value.name: Asha retrieves trial documents
value.description: Asha opens the drawer and takes out the trial record and intake log without asking.
evidence: she drew out the trial record and the intake log without asking and set them on the blotter beside the page he had not yet released

value.name: Asha rearranges documents to correct the order
value.description: She aligns the documents so the timestamps appear in the clerk-stamped order rather than the order she had previously given Whitfield.
evidence: She aligned the corners against the edge of the desk so the timestamps ran in the order the clerk had stamped them, not the order she had given him an hour before
The Hatcher trial record sat to the left, the intake log to the right, and the four-eighteen stamp ran in the order the clerk had pressed it, not the order Asha had given Whitfield an hour before

value.name: Asha steps back and lets Whitfield read
value.description: After arranging the papers, Asha steps back and leaves Whitfield to interpret the documents himself.
evidence: she stepped back and put her hands at her sides again
she stepped back the half pace that turned the desk into something he had to read rather than something she was handing him

value.name: Whitfield studies the arranged pages
value.description: Whitfield looks from the trial record to the intake log and then to Asha, absorbing the implication of her arrangement.
evidence: Whitfield looked at the second document and then at the third, and only then at her
Whitfield's eyes moved across the three pages in the sequence she had laid them in

value.name: Whitfield lifts his finger from the intake sheet
value.description: As he processes the corrected order, Whitfield's finger rises off the intake sheet and remains suspended.
evidence: his finger, which had been flat against the intake sheet, lifted clear of the paper and stayed lifted

value.name: Asha withholds an easier explanation
value.description: Asha deliberately avoids offering a sentence that would make her correction easier for Whitfield to accept.
evidence: did not offer the sentence that would have made the correction easier for him to receive

value.name: Asha waits for Whitfield's judgment to settle
value.description: Asha remains still and waits, knowing Whitfield's later judgment will be shaped by this moment.
evidence: She waited, because the version of her judgment he carried into the one o'clock would be built partly out
